classification.rationale: Interview transcript contains extraordinary claims about remote viewing, alien bases, UFO control, and military psychic programs. Custody unclear (podcast host), and content warrants human review for veracity and potential disinformation.

primary_claims: Lyn Buchanan had one of the highest clearances, not only for remote viewing but for other stuff that will never be talked about.
He remote viewed four major alien bases on Earth: Mount Hayes, Alaska; Mount Zeal in Australia; a secret mountain near Bradshaw Ranch in Sedona, Arizona; and Mount Inyangani.
He has seen humans and aliens working side by side in a non-remote viewing capacity, including insectoids sitting in a row of humans operating equipment.
He saw a UFO inside a hangar, encountered a control panel with finger holes, and learned to fly it from an alien pilot.
He can change the weather anywhere in the world.
He can access people mentally, demonstrated by telling the host 'the ignition sequence start' mentally.
As an Army sergeant in Augsburg, Germany, he fried an entire field station's computers (est. $50 million damage) in anger, also knocking out Russian computers in East Germany; this is documented.
General Stubblebine (INSCOM) recruited him for a unit to destroy/control enemy computers; when Congress refused funding, he was placed in the remote viewing unit at Fort Meade.
The remote viewing unit had existed for 10 years before he arrived, using Ingo Swann's controlled remote viewing method.

He remote viewed Saddam Hussein almost daily, finding him crazy and believing God wanted him to rule the world; he also discovered a hidden weapons bunker under a hollow generator at Saddam's personal compound.
Military remote viewers were forbidden to use skills against U.S. citizens or for personal reasons, only for tasked targets.
Public remote viewing teachings cover only about 1/10th of the knowledge (stages 1-6 of 18); Ingo Swann offered to teach him up to stage 11.
Another sergeant actually killed a goat psychically, experienced dying with the goat, and subsequently stole a helicopter and disappeared; this was not Buchanan.
The Soviet Union inherited German psychic spy programs after WWII, and by the 1960s were stealing classified information via psychic means; the U.S. started its program in response.
A single remote viewer can kill easily, but world leaders are not targeted because intelligence agencies prefer known actors over unknown replacements.
The host says the movie 'The Men Who Stare at Goats' was inspired by Buchanan, but Buchanan clarifies the goat-killing was another sergeant.
key_findings: Claim of U.S. military remote viewing program ongoing since the 1970s, with Buchanan active at Fort Meade.
Specification of four alien base locations, matching earlier Pat Price remote viewing claims (Mount Hayes, Mount Zeal, Sedona area, Mount Inyangani).
Assertion of physical UFO encounter inside a hangar and direct interaction with an alien pilot.
Assertion of large-scale computer destruction incident in Augsburg attributed to his psychokinesis, with alleged documentation.
Personal remote viewing of Saddam Hussein's mental state and hidden weapons bunker.
Mention of Ingo Swann's developmental stages (up to 18) and limited public dissemination.
Reference to a psychic goat-killing incident by another soldier, leading to that soldier's desertion.
Historical framing of German-Russian-U.S. psychic warfare lineage from WWII.
supporting_evidence: Interviewee's personal testimony as a former Army remote viewer under General Stubblebine.
Assertion that the Augsburg computer incident is 'documented' (unspecified documentation).
Names and locations provided with specificity (military unit, base, locations).
Consistency with some publicly known elements of the Stargate Project and Ingo Swann's remote viewing protocols.
Host's identification of the guest as inspiration for character in 'The Men Who Stare at Goats' (though guest partially distances).
contradictory_evidence: No independent verification of any claims within the source text.
The alien base locations are identical to those attributed to remote viewer Pat Price in the 1970s (as reported in secondary literature), suggesting possible narrative recycling or circular sourcing.
No official documents, military records, or witness corroboration provided.
follow_up_needed: Verify Lyn Buchanan's identity, service record, and security clearance history through FOIA requests or official military archives.
Investigate the Augsburg field station computer incident (date, unit, any official reports or news) to test the documentation claim.
Cross-reference the alien base locations with Pat Price's original session transcripts; determine if Buchanan is independently reporting or repeating known material.
Seek corroboration from other remote viewers or personnel from the Fort Meade unit regarding his claimed tasks (Saddam Hussein, UFO hangar).
Assess whether the hangar UFO/alien narrative appears in other sources and if it matches any known hoax patterns.
Next Trace: Locate the alleged 'documented' record of the computer incident or any official acknowledgment of Buchanan's involvement with INSCOM remote viewing unit.
content_assessment.notes: Guest makes multiple extraordinary claims but provides no verifiable evidence. Several elements (alien base locations) are recycled from earlier remote viewing lore. The interview format lacks independent fact-checking. Classification-aware reading: None of the claims bear official classification marks; the mere assertion of 'highest clearances' is unverifiable. Until independent documentation surfaces, the content is not admissible as factual intelligence.
